Seeing companions only pass wet hands over their feet in ablution for an overdue prayer, the Prophet called out loudly to save their heels from the fire.
Seeing companions only pass wet hands over their feet in ablution for an overdue Asr prayer, the Prophet called out loudly to save their heels from the fire.
Too shy to ask himself, Ali had Al-Miqdad ask about frequent urethral discharge, and the Prophet said it requires ablution.
Prayer after hadath needs ablution, whose traces will make the Prophet's followers shine on Resurrection Day, and one who doubts in prayer leaves only on hearing or smelling something.
The Prophet prayed after sleeping without new ablution, made a light ablution after Arafat and a full one at Muzdalifa, and Ibn Abbas demonstrated his ablution handful by handful.
The Prophet washed the limbs once or twice, and Uthman, washing thrice, reported that such an ablution followed by an attentive prayer brings forgiveness of sins.
Ablution includes rinsing the nose and, after sleep, washing the hands before dipping them; stones are used in odd numbers, and unwashed heels are threatened with the Fire.
Waiting in the mosque counts as prayer until hadath, doubt requires a sound or smell, and urethral discharge and intercourse without emission were each said to need ablution.
Usama poured water for the Prophet's ablution after Arafat, and Al-Mughira on a journey, when he wiped over his head and khuffs.
Asked to show the Prophet's ablution, Abdullah bin Zaid rinsed mouth and nose and washed his face thrice, forearms twice, wiped his head back and forth, and washed his feet.
Abdullah bin Zaid again showed the Prophet's ablution from a pot, and Ibn Umar said men and women made ablution together in the Prophet's lifetime.
The Prophet washed his hands and face in a tumbler and threw in a mouthful, and made ablution from a brass pot, washing his face thrice and forearms twice.
Asked by a man who used too much water, Abdullah bin Zaid showed the Prophet's ablution from an earthenware pot, rinsing mouth and nose thrice from one handful.
The Prophet used a sa' to five mudds of water for bathing and one mudd for ablution, and companions saw him wipe over his khuffs and once his turban.
The Prophet prayed without new ablution after eating cooked mutton, and after saweeq only rinsed his mouth, as he did after milk, saying it has fat.
The Prophet made ablution for every prayer while companions kept one until hadath, and after eating saweeq he only rinsed his mouth before praying.
Ali had a man ask the Prophet about frequent urethral discharge, and was told to wash the organ and make ablution.
Uthman washed his hands, mouth, nose, face, arms and feet as the Prophet did, who promised forgiveness of past sins to one praying two undistracted rak'at after such ablution.
After relieving himself, the Prophet made ablution in a tight-sleeved Sha'mi cloak, drawing his arms out from beneath it, and wiped over his head and leather socks.
The Prophet ate from a sheep's shoulder, cutting it with a knife, then put the knife down when called and prayed without repeating his ablution.
On a journey the Prophet made ablution in a narrow-sleeved cloak, drawing his arms out from beneath it, and wiped over his Khuffs, worn after ablution.
Uthman performed ablution as the Prophet did, who said such ablution followed by two rak'at in the mosque forgives past sins, but warned against being conceited about it.
Allah does not accept the prayer of one who has passed wind until he performs ablution anew.
